headline: Every major is stretched above its 200-day line while whales quietly walk coins onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it's about as clean as this tape ever gets: six of seven majors sit above their 200-day trendline. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE are all in that camp, with ADA the lone holdout, sitting 76.6% off its 12-month high and still under its 200-day. That's a market where the broad trend is up almost everywhere, which is rarer than it sounds and worth noting plainly rather than celebrating.

But trend and momentum are telling two different stories right now, and that gap is the first real finding. RSI readings across the board are hot: BTC at 79.7, ETH 78.5, SOL 80.6, XRP 79.8, BNB 82.1, DOGE 76.6. Those are textbook overbought numbers, the kind that usually accompany a market running faster than its own fuel supply. MACD is still above signal on every asset, so the accelerator is technically down, but everything on the 24-hour tape is red: BTC -0.29%, ETH -0.17%, SOL -1.02%, XRP -2.96%, BNB -0.47%, DOGE -2.86%, ADA -3.98%. That's a market with a strong multi-week trend (BTC is up 23.01% over 7 days and 21.56% over 30) taking a breather on the daily candle, momentum indicators still stretched from the run, not yet rolling over. Call it resting, not reversing, but the divergence between the weekly strength and the daily softness is exactly what a reader should be watching.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE is uniformly at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized) on OKX, which is unremarkable, not the kind of expensive, crowded funding that usually precedes a flush. But the long/short account ratios tell a different story depending on the asset: BTC's near balanced at 1.05, ETH modestly long-skewed at 1.14, while SOL (1.94), XRP (2.09) and especially DOGE (3.24) show the crowd heavily stacked long. Liquidations over the past day lean short-side on BTC ($5.3M shorts vs $4.6M longs) and heavily short-side on ETH ($7.9M shorts vs $3.1M longs), meaning the squeeze so far has hurt bears more than bulls, even as today's spot tape sits in the red. Cheap funding plus long-skewed crowds on the smaller-cap alts is a setup that's fragile if price actually turns, since there's more long exposure to unwind than short.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. On the ETF side, BTC spot funds took in $307.5M on 21 Aug, part of a five-session net of $1,917.8M with all five days pointing the same direction, a real and traceable institutional bid. ETH ETFs echoed it: $184.0M on the day, $692.6M over five sessions, also five-for-five same direction. That's traditional finance buying. Set against it, whale wallets moved $132.4M net onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, led by BTC ($107.5M net onto exchanges, including two single blocks of $133.3M and $62.6M landing at Binance) and a $24.9M TRUMP token deposit, also to Binance. Zoom out to the weekly series and the onto-exchange trend has been building for three straight weeks: $42M the week ending Aug 10, $473M the week ending Aug 17, $1,091M the week ending Aug 24, a reversal from the $1,154M that moved off exchanges in the week ending Aug 03. Coins moving toward exchanges typically precedes distribution, and it's happening in the same window that ETF buyers are stepping in. Two different types of participants pulling in opposite directions is the honest read here, not a contradiction to explain away.

Sentiment sits at 73, Greed, right at the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 73. The crowd feels as good as it has felt all month, which lines up with the RSI readings but sits awkwardly next to the whale data quietly building exchange balances. Stablecoin float is essentially flat, up just 0.01% over 30 days to $308.6B, so there's no fresh sideline cash rushing in to meet potential selling. Total market cap fell 1.67% over the past 24 hours to $2.62T, with BTC dominance at 59.3%, consistent with the red day across majors even as weekly trends stay firmly higher.

What to watch from here: whether the onto-exchange whale flow extends into a fourth straight week, whether ETF net flows break their five-day same-direction streak, and whether funding on the long-skewed alts (SOL, XRP, DOGE) stays cheap or starts climbing as those crowded long positions get more expensive to hold. A flip in any of those three would be the kind of concrete change worth flagging, rather than reading into a single red day of price action.
